search_results.replace_tooltip: Replaces the query found in the selected result with the text in the field above
search_results.replace_all_tooltip: Replaces all occurrences of the query in the current editor with the text in the field above
search_results.section_search_doc_tooltip:
Search the currently open document in the editor.
Results are listed in the tree below.
Choose the mode: plain text, regular expression (.*) or SQL LIKE (%LIKE%).
Press Enter or the 'Search' button to start.
search_results.search_doc_tooltip:
Enter the text to search in the currently open document.

In TEXT mode the search is smart (AND/NOT):
  jira prob        → lines with BOTH words (AND)
  jira -prob       → lines with 'jira' but NOT 'prob' (-word or !word = NOT)
  java error null  → lines containing all 3 words

Note: switch to .* mode to search for literals like '-v' or '!important'

Other modes (dropdown):
• .* — Python regular expression (e.g. \bfoo\b, [A-Z]+, foo.*bar)
• %LIKE% — SQL LIKE syntax (% = any sequence, _ = one character; e.g. %foo%)

Options:
• Aa — case-sensitive
• \b — whole word only

Press Enter or the 'Search' button to start.
search_results.search_mode_tooltip:
Search mode in the document:
• text — smart multi-word search:
   space = AND (all words must be present)
   -word or !word = NOT (word must NOT be present)
   Ex: 'jira prob' → lines with jira AND prob
   Ex: 'jira -prob' → lines with jira but NOT prob
   (use .* mode to search for literals like '-v' or '!important')
• .* — Python regular expression
   Ex: \bdef\s+\w+ finds all function definitions
• %LIKE% — SQL LIKE syntax
   % = any sequence of characters
   _ = exactly one character
   Ex: %Error% finds everything containing 'Error'
search_results.search_whole_word_tooltip:
Search whole words only (word boundary).
Ex: 'foo' does not match 'foobar' or 'barfoo', only 'foo' as a standalone word.
search_results.section_filter_tooltip:
Live-filter the results already shown in the tree, without running a new search.
This is a secondary filter: shows only lines matching the entered text.
Supports grep (AND/NOT), Python regexp, and SQL LIKE modes.
search_results.filter_tooltip:
Quick filter on results already found (live, as you type).

grep mode (default):
  Space-separated words = AND (all must be present)
  -word or !word = NOT (excludes lines with that word)
  Ex: 'error -warning' → lines with 'error' but without 'warning'
  Ex: 'foo bar' → lines containing both 'foo' and 'bar'

.* mode (Python regexp):
  Use standard Python regular expressions
  Ex: '^def ' finds lines starting with 'def '

%LIKE% mode (SQL LIKE):
  % = any sequence, _ = one character
  Ex: '%Error%' finds everything containing 'Error'
search_results.filter_mode_tooltip:
Filter mode for results:
• grep — AND/NOT with space-separated words (-word = NOT)
• .* — Python regular expression
• %LIKE% — SQL LIKE syntax (% = any sequence, _ = one character)
search_results.search_case_tooltip:
Case-sensitive search.
When active: 'Foo' and 'foo' are treated as different words.
search_results.search_regex_tooltip: Search using a regular expression (Python regex)
search_results.btn_search_tooltip:
Start searching in the currently open document.
Results replace the previous ones.
Works like 'Find all' but integrated in this panel.
search_results.append_results_tooltip:
If active, new search results are APPENDED to the existing ones,
without clearing previous searches.
You can see the history of all searches performed.
Click on a previous search title (blue row) to restore its parameters in the fields.

tooltip.ai_provider:
Choose the AI service to use.
Each provider requires its own API key (except Ollama, which runs locally).
tooltip.ai_model:
Model to use for the response.
Larger models (Opus, GPT-4o) are more capable but slower and more expensive.
Flash/mini models are faster and cheaper for simple tasks.
tooltip.ai_settings:
Open settings to configure API keys.
Each provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini) requires a separate key.
Ollama requires no key.
tooltip.ai_thinking:
Enable Claude's extended reasoning (Opus 4.7 and Sonnet 4.5-thinking).

With this option enabled, the model 'thinks' before answering:
it analyzes the problem from multiple angles and produces more accurate responses
for math, logic, complex code and planning.

Downside: uses many more tokens and the response arrives more slowly.
tooltip.ai_cost:
Estimated cost per 1 million input and output tokens.
Actual cost depends on conversation length.
tooltip.ai_system:
Open/close the System Prompt field.

The system prompt is a permanent instruction the model follows
throughout the conversation, before any user message.

Useful examples:
  • «Always respond in English»
  • «You are a Python expert. Be concise.»
  • «Never use bullet points in responses»
tooltip.ai_ask_file:
Inserts the entire open file as context in the input field,
then moves the cursor to the end so you can write your question.

Use this button when you want to ask something about the current file,
for example: «Explain this function» or «Are there bugs here?»
tooltip.ai_ask_sel:
Inserts only the selected text from the editor as context.
If nothing is selected, uses the entire file.

Select a function or block, then click here
and write the specific question about that fragment.
tooltip.ai_explain:
Sends the selected code (or the file) with a request
to explain it clearly and in detail.
tooltip.ai_refactor:
Asks the AI to rewrite the code improving
readability and structure without changing behavior.
tooltip.ai_docstring:
Generates a professional docstring (parameters, return,
examples) for the selected function or class.
tooltip.ai_fix_bug:
Analyzes the code for bugs and proposes
the corrected version with explanation of errors found.
tooltip.ai_more:
Opens a menu with more contextual actions:
Optimize, Unit tests, Review, Translate comments…
tooltip.ai_input:
Message input field.
You can type freely or use the buttons above
to automatically insert code as context.

Ctrl+Enter — send the message
tooltip.ai_add_context:
Adds the selected text (or the entire file if nothing is selected)
directly at the cursor position in the input field.

Useful for adding context in the middle of an already-written message.
tooltip.ai_clear:
Clears the entire conversation history and starts fresh.
The AI will not remember previous messages after this action.
tooltip.ai_send:
Send the message to the AI and wait for the response.
Shortcut: Ctrl+Enter from the input field.
tooltip.ai_apply:
Replaces the active editor content with the last AI response.
If the response contains exactly one code block, it is extracted automatically;
otherwise the full text is used.

The operation can be undone with Ctrl+Z.
tooltip.ai_new_tab:
Opens the last AI response in a new empty tab.
Contains the full response text, including explanation and code.
tooltip.ai_inline:
Inline edit mode: after sending, the AI response
automatically replaces the current selection in the editor
(or the entire file if nothing is selected).

If the response contains exactly one code block, it is extracted automatically.
tooltip.git_pull:
git pull — Download and integrate changes from remote.
Keeps the local repo in sync with the server.
tooltip.git_push:
git push — Upload local commits to remote.
Requires at least one configured remote (e.g. origin).
tooltip.git_commit:
git add . + git commit — Opens a dialog to choose
which files to include and write the commit message.
tooltip.git_stash:
Yes → git stash push  (save uncommitted changes)
No → git stash pop   (restore saved changes)
tooltip.find_regex_help:
Regular expression (Python re):
  .       any character
  \d      digit  |  \w  word char  |  \s  space
  *       0 or more  |  +  1 or more  |  ?  0 or 1
  ^       line start  |  $  line end
  [abc]   character class  |  [^abc]  negation
  (...)   group  |  (?:...)  non-capturing group
  \1      back-reference to group 1
  a|b     alternation (a or b)
  \b      word boundary

In Replace field: \1 \2 ... for captured groups
